Descriptions.Text: No special behaviour: only the effect's own fields apply.
No built-in effect. Only TAE events gated on this state react to it (a c0000 SFX and a c5050 sound), and no vanilla row sets it, so a mod row with this state switches those events on.

The poison ailment. Shows in the first status-ailment slot (timer = the effect's remaining duration) with the POISON banner, flags poison for HKS (STATUS_EFFECT_POISON), and is removed by cure states 10 and 13 and by the cure-all (grace rest, respawn). The damage itself comes from the row's changeHpPoint/changeHpRate ticking every motionInterval.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Only a test row uses it; any effect comes from the row's own fields.

The row's insideDurability is applied to the durability of every weapon slot and armour piece when the effect is applied (positive values wear, negative values repair). Weapons flagged to ignore durability changes are skipped, and the row is skipped entirely if it has corrosionIgnore set.

The scarlet rot ailment. Shows in the second status-ailment slot with the SCARLET ROT banner, flags rot for HKS (STATUS_EFFECT_DEADLY_POISON), and is removed by cure states 11 and 13 and by the cure-all. The damage comes from the row's HP-change fields.

The blood loss (hemorrhage) ailment. Shows in the third status-ailment slot with the BLOOD LOSS banner, flags bleed for HKS (STATUS_EFFECT_BLOOD), and is removed by cure states 12 and 13 and by the cure-all. The burst damage comes from the row's own fields.

The row's hearing modifiers (hearingSearchEnemyAdd/Rate) never apply, and its sight modifiers (sightSearchEnemyAdd/Rate) only apply to AI sight checks that ask for camouflage effects. Pairs with 53. No vanilla row uses it.

Marks the character as hidden or vanished. The game does not test it; AI scripts do (spirit candle enemies stop walking while it is active). Any effect on enemy sight comes from the row's own sight fields.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
When applied, removes all active poison (state 2) effects, then ends itself immediately.
When applied, removes all active scarlet rot (state 5) effects, then ends itself immediately.
When applied, removes all active blood loss (state 6) effects, then ends itself immediately.
When applied, removes poison (2), scarlet rot (5), blood loss (6), frostbite (260), maggots (261), sleep (436) and madness (437), then ends itself immediately. Used by grace rest and respawn.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Any effect comes from the row's own fields.
Puts the player camera into its zoom (scope) mode, the same mode as aiming, for as long as the effect is active. HKS act(120) ends this state, and HKS env(305, 15) tests it.
When active on the player, requests the Darksign warp (warp kind 1, the pseudo-multiplayer return position path). A leftover from older games.
Revives the player in place: runs the same restore as respawning (HP and FP set to maximum, mount and equipment state refreshed), then shows text banner 2000.
While active on the player, fires the OnBeBlackKickOut script event (a dark phantom being sent home). No vanilla row uses it.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
While active on the player, fires the OnReviveMagic script event. No vanilla row uses it.
The character may not use magic while active (checked for enemies), unless another active effect has antiMagicIgnore set. No vanilla row uses it.

The row's insideDurability is applied to the active weapon only, when the effect is applied (positive values wear, negative values repair). The change applies even to a broken weapon; see 292 for the variant that skips broken ones.
A label for the war cry attack buffs. The game does not test it; other effects use it as an invocation condition. The buff itself is the row's own fields.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by body-protection incantations; the protection is the rows' own fields.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Any effect comes from the row's own fields.

Marks the character as bound or paralysed. AI can test it (the Lua HasParalysis function and target checks), and HKS env(362, 32) tests it in behaviour scripts. The immobility itself comes from the row's own fields and animations.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Only a prototype row uses it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Only a prototype row uses it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Only a prototype row uses it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Only a prototype row uses it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Only a test row uses it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by upper-tier protection incantations; the protection is the rows' own fields.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by fire protection incantations; the protection is the rows' own fields.
A marker for enemy and spirit heals. The game does not test it; only TAE attack events gated on it react (c3360).
First step of a three-stage ladder (43, 44, 45). A new 43 is refused while 43, 44 or 45 is already active. No vanilla row uses it.
Second step of the 43-44-45 ladder. It can only be applied while 43 is active (and not while 44 or 45 is), and it ends 43 when it is applied. No vanilla row uses it.
Third step of the 43-44-45 ladder. It can only be applied while 44 is active (and not while 43 is), and it ends 43 and 44 when it is applied. No vanilla row uses it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Any effect comes from the row's own fields.
The character takes no fall damage, and does not die from falls, while active. HKS also tests it (CAT_LANDING) to choose landing animations.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by low-HP attack boosts; the condition and the bonus are the rows' own fields.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by low-HP defense boosts; the condition and the bonus are the rows' own fields.

A regeneration effect: when applied (and when reapplied), its tick timer starts with a full motionInterval already counted, so the first HP/FP change happens at once instead of after one interval. Used by grace restores and regen buffs.
Same as 50: the tick timer starts with a full motionInterval already counted, so the first tick happens at once.
Same as 7: the row's hearing modifiers never apply, and its sight modifiers only apply to AI sight checks that ask for camouflage effects. No vanilla row uses it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by silencing effects; the silence is the rows' own hearing fields.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by a system row only.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by the point-light equipment system row; the light is the row's own fields.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by the message appraisal restore row.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by weapon greases; the buff is the rows' own fields.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by greases; the buff is the rows' own fields.
A label for fire and blood-flame weapon buffs. The game does not test it; only TAE events gated on it react (c4310, c4340).
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by magic greases; the buff is the rows' own fields.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
While active, the itemDropRate of every active effect (not just this one) is added to item discovery. Without a state-66 effect, itemDropRate does nothing.
Same as 50: the tick timer starts with a full motionInterval already counted, so the first tick happens at once. No vanilla row uses it.
Same as 50: the tick timer starts with a full motionInterval already counted, so the first tick happens at once. No vanilla row uses it.
Selects death-penalty mode 1 (the event lost-runes restriction) when the player dies with it active, taking priority over 159 and 160. Dying of death blight (117) ignores it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Only a test row uses it.
A marker used for TAE gating and as an invocation condition for other effects. The game does not test it.
A marker used for TAE gating and as an invocation condition for other effects. The game does not test it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by stamina-recovery boosts; the bonus is the rows' own fields.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by rune-gain boosts; the bonus is the rows' own fields.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Only a prototype row uses it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Only a prototype row uses it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Only a prototype row uses it.

Mimic's Veil. When it starts, the character takes one of three disguise forms, picked at random with the weights mimicryEstablishment0-2 of the area's MapMimicryEstablishmentParam row (row 0 if none); each form uses that row's begin/loop/end SFX. States 509, 510 and 511 each rule out one form. The form is kept until the effect ends, and some AI and lock-on logic is skipped while it is active.

Replaces the character's armour look with the effect's SpEffectVfx transformProtectorId (full body or gauntlets as that row says) while active, and locks the head slot in the equipment menu. 167 is the full-body version that locks all slots.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
No built-in effect. HKS env(269) returns whether it is active, so behaviour scripts can react to it. Removed by cure state 104. No vanilla row or script uses it.
No built-in effect. HKS env(270) returns whether it is active, so behaviour scripts can react to it. No vanilla row or script uses it.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
The player counts as overloaded (heaviest equip-load category) whatever their equipment weight, while active. No vanilla row uses it.

Makes the effect conditional even when its row has no HP or state conditions: it is re-checked every tick, switching on while its conditions pass and waiting (or ending, with isWaitModeDelete) while they fail. No vanilla row uses it.
When applied, removes states 99, 105, 106 and 107, then ends itself immediately. No vanilla row uses it.
The base level of a three-step replace ladder (105, 106, 107). Removed by 104, 106 and 107. No vanilla row uses it.
Replace level 1 for replaceCategory 1: when applied it removes 105, and it stays active for its duration. Removed by 104 and 107. No vanilla row uses it.
Replace level 2 for replaceCategory 1: when applied it removes 105 and 106, and it stays active for its duration. Removed by 104. No vanilla row uses it.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Counts as state 107 for the replace-level checks. No vanilla row uses it.
The row's damage-cut rates (physical per attack type, magic, fire, lightning, holy) apply only to counter hits instead of every hit. Used by counter-damage effects.
First step of a five-stage ladder (111, 112, 113, 114, 192). A new 111 is refused while any higher stage is active; cure state 198 removes the whole ladder. No vanilla row uses it.
Second step of the 111-192 ladder: refused while 113, 114 or 192 is active, and ends 111 when applied. Cure 198 removes it. No vanilla row uses it.
Third step of the 111-192 ladder: refused while 114 or 192 is active, and ends 111-112 when applied. Cure 198 removes it. No vanilla row uses it.

Fourth step of the 111-192 ladder: refused while 192 is active, and ends 111-113 when applied. While active it also unequips the head and locks the head slot, and applies the effect's armour transformation as 96 does. Cure 198 removes it. No vanilla row uses it.
While active, a player with light enough equipment drops into an extra-light equip-load category (below the normal light category). No vanilla row uses it.

The death blight ailment. Shows in the fourth status-ailment slot with the DEATH BLIGHTED banner, flags blight for HKS (STATUS_EFFECT_CURSE), and is removed by cure state 118 and by the cure-all. Its rows replace themselves with 117 (the instant death) when the build-up completes.
The instant death caused by death blight. The fourth ailment slot shows it as full; dying with it active ignores every death-penalty protection (69, 159, 160). The cure-all ends it.
When applied, removes death blight build-up (116); it stays active for its duration rather than ending at once.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Any effect comes from the row's own fields.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by effects that change damage animations under super armor; the change is the rows' own dmgLv fields.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by behaviour effects (stance stabilisation, damage animation changes); the change is the rows' own dmgLv fields.

The effect only works while the character stands in water or a shallow swamp (HitMtrlParam floors 19-23 and 60); on any other floor it is suspended, and it resumes when the character steps back in. No vanilla row uses it.
The row's attack power is added as a separate contact-damage source, only to hits whose contact type includes the head piece's bits (used by the Briar set's rolling damage).
The row's attack power is added as a separate contact-damage source, only to hits whose contact type includes the body piece's bits (used by the Briar set and Mantle of Thorns).
The row's attack power is added as a separate contact-damage source, only to hits whose contact type includes the arms piece's bits (four kinds of contact).
The row's attack power is added as a separate contact-damage source, only to hits whose contact type includes the legs piece's bits (three kinds of contact).
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.

Charms the character (Bewitching Branch): AI treats it as charmed and is reset when the charm starts and ends, and the row's changeTeamType switches its side. The charm only takes on targets that already have an active effect with enableCharm set; on anyone else the effect is refused.
Widens the radius at which bloodstain messages appear around the player to 5 m (fully faded by 6 m), instead of the normal radius.
Replaces the character's defence material with iron (material 106) while active, so hits produce metal sounds and sparks. Used by living jars and Ironjar Aromatic.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
No built-in effect. Behaviour scripts test it (CONDITION_TYPE_CRYSTAL). No vanilla row uses it.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Replace level 1 for items and spells with replaceCategory 2: while active, those items or spells use their first replacement. No vanilla row uses it.
Replace level 2 for items and spells with replaceCategory 2: while active, those items or spells use their second replacement. No vanilla row uses it.
Replace level 3 for items and spells with replaceCategory 2: while active, those items or spells use their third replacement. No vanilla row uses it.
Replace level 4 for items and spells with replaceCategory 2: while active, those items or spells use their fourth replacement. No vanilla row uses it.
When applied, runs the row's behaviorId as a behaviour on the character. Used by lava and burn hits.

The character can't die while active: HP stops at the minimum instead of reaching death, so scripted revivals (one-time revival enemies) can play. HKS env(1101) tests the same can't-die check, and HKS env(362, 143) tests the state.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
No built-in effect. Behaviour scripts test it (env 305, SP_EFFECT_TYPE_HOLY). No vanilla row uses it.
Like 4: the row's insideDurability is applied to every weapon slot and armour piece when the effect is applied, but corrosionIgnore does not exempt it. No vanilla row uses it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by light sources (torches, lanterns, Starlight); the light is the rows' own antiDarkSightRadius.
Used by the help-request system rows. The only check reads it and throws the result away, so it has no effect in this build.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by lightning weapon buffs; the buff is the rows' own fields.

A weapon buff whose atkOccurrenceSpEffectId is applied when its attacks hit. Only the first active 152/153 effect that fits the attack is used; atkOccurrenceSpEffectId does nothing on rows with other states.
Same as 152: the first active 152/153 effect that fits the attack supplies the on-hit SpEffect (atkOccurrenceSpEffectId). No vanilla row uses it.
The player can't use the refillable flasks (goods with suppleType 1 or 2) while active. Behaviour scripts also test it (CONDITION_TYPE_NO_EST).
The row's changeSuperArmorPoint takes effect only on rows with this state; nothing else reads that field. Used by super-armor casting effects.
While active, changes to equipment maximum durability (from maxDurability on applied effects) are skipped. TAE events gated on it exist (c4450), but no vanilla row uses it.
The character's attacks can hit enemies flagged isGhost in NpcParam, which they would otherwise pass through. It also changes how the character is treated as a defender (not yet understood).

The row's guard fields (guardDefFlickPowerRate, guardStaminaCutRate, guardStaminaMult) take effect only on rows with this state (or 204/470 for the last two). Used by the Barricade Shield hardness buffs.

When the player dies with it active, the death penalty is avoided (runes are not lost) and the Sacrificial Twig in a talisman slot is used up. Overridden by 69 and 160, and ignored when dying of death blight.
When the player dies with it active, the death penalty is avoided without using anything up (Twiggy Cracked Tear). Takes priority over 159; overridden by 69; ignored when dying of death blight.
A cut return-stone warp kind. Its handler is empty, so it does nothing in ER.
A cut return-stone warp kind. Its handler is empty, so it does nothing in ER.
A cut return-stone warp kind. Its handler is empty, so it does nothing in ER.
A cut return-stone warp kind. Its handler is empty, so it does nothing in ER.
A cut return-stone warp kind. Its handler is empty, so it does nothing in ER.
While active on the player, clears their covenant (vow) unless the covenant is locked.

Locks every armour slot in the equipment menu while active. The transformed look comes from the effect's SpEffectVfx transformProtectorId (with isFullBodyTransformProtectorId). Used by Rock Heart, Priestess Heart and Lamenter's Mask. See 96 for the head-only version.

Removes the lower zoom limit of the scope camera (bow aiming, telescope), so the whole zoom range is available. Arrow's Reach uses it; its bow-range bonus is the separate bowDistRate field, which counts on any effect.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
While active, damage taken is added to the retribution total that triggers the chained effect (Law of Causality). The chained row uses this state as its condition.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Only a test row uses it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Any effect comes from the row's own fields.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by system rows (revival effect, ritual target).
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by catnip rows; the effect is the rows' own AI sound and target priority fields.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by catnip rows; the effect is the rows' own AI sound and target priority fields.

Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by Unseen Blade; the effect is the row's own fields.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Like 123-126: the row's attack power is added as a separate contact-damage source, only to hits whose contact type matches (two kinds of contact). No vanilla row uses it.
No built-in effect, but a large set of c0000 TAE events (attacks, SFX and sounds) only play while it is active, which unlocks the weapon's special moveset effects.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by a system row only.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by a system row only.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.

Top step of the 111-192 ladder: ends 111-114 when applied, and none of them can be applied while it is active. While active it also unequips the head and locks the head slot, and applies the effect's armour transformation as 96 does. Cure 198 removes it. No vanilla row uses it.
While active, every effect flagged isExtendSpEffectLife lasts longer by this row's extendLifeRate (rates from several 193 effects add up). Used by the Old Lord's Talisman.
Casting a spell uses up two thirds of a use instead of one. ER spells have unlimited uses (FP pays instead), so it has no visible effect unless a spell sets maxQuantity.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by a system row only.
Tested on the player, but the code it triggers is empty in this build, so it does nothing.
The row's attack rates apply only to the character's counter hits. Used by the Spear Talisman.
When applied, removes states 111, 112, 113, 114 and 192, then ends itself immediately.

When the player defeats an enemy, every active effect with this state applies its applyIdOnGetSoul. applyIdOnGetSoul does nothing on rows with other states. Used by Rykard's Great Rune, Taker's Cameo and similar.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by self-buffs; the buff is the rows' own fields.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Casting a spell uses up two uses instead of one. ER spells have unlimited uses (FP pays instead), so it has no visible effect unless a spell sets maxQuantity.
Same as 158: the row's guard fields take effect only on rows with this state. No vanilla row uses it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by holy weapon buffs; the buff is the rows' own fields.
A marker used as the invocation condition for other effects (the Black Knife Assassin's hide). The game does not test it.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.

Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Marks the player as inside the Colosseum: goods with disableUseAtOutOfColiseum can only be used while it is active. No vanilla row sets it.
Like 143, but only for players: while active, the player can't die. HKS env(1101) tests the same can't-die check. No vanilla row uses it.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
The character is covered in oil: the next fire hit ignites it and ends the oil effect. The extra fire damage taken is the row's own fireDamageCutRate.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by the crouching-in-grass AI sound row.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by the downed-state row; AI scripts could test it but none do.

The frostbite ailment. Shows in the fifth status-ailment slot with the FROSTBITE banner, flags frostbite for HKS (STATUS_EFFECT_COLD), and is removed by cure states 13 and 276 and by the cure-all. A fire hit on a frostbitten character applies SpEffect 5247, which removes the frost.
A maggot infestation that bleeds the character through its cycle effect. Removed by cure states 262 and 13.
When applied, removes maggots (state 261), then ends itself immediately. Used by torches and the maggot-curing bolus.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by ritual-corpse rows.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by a quick-match timing system row.
No built-in effect; behaviour scripts test it (env 305, SP_EFFECT_TYPE_FALL_DEATH_INVALID) to stop forced fall deaths in certain maps.
The AI targeting system takes its sight-cone angles from this row's eye_angX and eye_angY while active. Those fields do nothing on rows with other states.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
A marker identifying spirit summons for TAE gating and as an invocation condition. The game does not test it.
A marker used as the invocation condition for another effect (a spirit's reserved damage-animation change). The game does not test it.
A marker used as the invocation condition for another effect (a spirit's reserved damage-animation change). The game does not test it.
When applied, runs the row's behaviorId as a behaviour from the row's dmypolyId on the character. Used by many behaviour attachments (Spiritspring jumps, ailment cycle searches).
When applied, removes frostbite (state 260), then ends itself immediately.
While active on the player, the equipped Great Rune is active.
While active, warp items, warp sorceries and incantations, and fast travel from the menu are refused.
Changes which summoning slot the multiplayer system opens for the player, which only matters for one cut covenant-style summon kind. No vanilla row uses it.
Unused: set on the player but only read by a multiplayer debug display, so it has no gameplay effect.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by wetness rows.

The effect only exists during multiplayer: it is removed whenever the player is not in an online session with other players. It is also left out of the active-effect list sent for other players. Used by multiplayer scaling.
While active, HP that reaches 0 is set back to 1, so the character can't be killed by HP loss. No vanilla row uses it.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used as a label by drain and heal-on-hit rows.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by a system notification row.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
A marker used as the invocation condition for the effect triggered by the Assassin's Crimson Dagger (critical hits restore HP). The game does not test it.
A marker used as the invocation condition for the effect triggered by the Assassin's Cerulean Dagger (critical hits restore FP). The game does not test it.
No built-in effect, but c0000 TAE events that extend roll invincibility only play while it is active. Used by the Crucible Feather Talisman and Windy Crystal Tear.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
The row's insideDurability changes the durability of the active weapon only (negative values repair), and only if the weapon wasn't already broken. No vanilla row uses it.
The row's insideDurability changes the durability of every weapon slot and armour piece (negative values repair), skipping pieces that are already broken. Used by the weapon repair row.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.
Unused: set on the player but only read by a multiplayer debug display, so it has no gameplay effect.
Nothing in Elden Ring sets or tests this value, so it has no effect.

The mark that the activity-of-dead search (318) leaves on a corpse. It only sticks to a ragdolled corpse that hasn't started fading, then makes the corpse fade out over GameSystemCommonParam activityOfDeadSpEffect_DeadFadeOutTime. Effects with this state are never sent to other players. No vanilla row uses it.
While active, the row's chrProxyHeightRate scales the character's collision height (used for the crouching stance).
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by a multiplayer host row.
Unused: nothing in the game tests this value. Used by a multiplayer guest row.
While active, every effect flagged isContractSpEffectLife runs out faster by this row's contractLifeRate (rates from several 301 effects add up). Used by Law of Regression.
When active on the player, warps them using the return-stone warp; the destination kind is chosen by the game's warp system.

Enables accumulator gauge 1: effects with accumuVal add to this gauge only while a 303 effect is active, and the gauge never drops below 0. The 303 row's accumuOverFireId / accumuUnderFireId fire when the gauge crosses accumuOverVal / accumuUnderVal. Also used widely as an enemy TAE marker.

Enables accumulator gauge 2: effects with accumuVal add to it only while a 304 effect is active (never below 0), and the row's over/under fire IDs trigger at its thresholds. Also used as an enemy TAE marker.

Enables accumulator gauge 3: effects with accumuVal add to it only while a 305 effect is active (never below 0), and the row's over/under fire IDs trigger at its thresholds. Also used as an enemy TAE marker.

Enables accumulator gauge 4: effects with accumuVal add to it only while a 306 effect is active (never below 0), and the row's over/under fire IDs trigger at its thresholds. Also used as an enemy TAE marker.

Enables accumulator gauge 5: effects with accumuVal add to it only while a 307 effect is active (never below 0), and the row's over/under fire IDs trigger at its thresholds. Also used as an enemy TAE marker and by AI scripts.

Enables accumulator gauge 6: effects with accumuVal add to it only while a 308 effect is active (never below 0), and the row's over/under fire IDs trigger at its thresholds. Used by the Thorny Cracked Tear gauge.
Enables accumulator gauge 7: effects with accumuVal add to it only while a 309 effect is active (never below 0), and the row's over/under fire IDs trigger at its thresholds. Used by Festive Grease.
Enables accumulator gauge 8: effects with accumuVal add to it only while a 310 effect is active (never below 0), and the row's over/under fire IDs trigger at its thresholds. Used by Festive Grease.
Enables accumulator gauge 9: effects with accumuVal add to it only while a 311 effect is active (never below 0), and the row's over/under fire IDs trigger at its thresholds.

Enables accumulator gauge 10: effects with accumuVal add to it only while a 312 effect is active (never below 0), and the row's over/under fire IDs trigger at its thresholds. Used by Malenia's rot support.
While active, summon signs are shown to the player as if the Furlcalling Finger Remedy were in use. Used by the cycled Scriptstone.
When applied, adds the row's accumuVal to the accumulator gauges in one go (for gauges whose slot state is active).
The row's attack rates are scaled by a curve (CalcCorrectGraph 50) of the player's equip load, so the bonus is largest at low load. Used by the Blue Dancer Charm.
Same as 315, using CalcCorrectGraph 51 for the curve.
